blocks.x: Equipment makers pivot to outcome businesses: connected machines, service contracts and uptime guarantees replace box sales. The pivot is an engineering program — fleet connectivity, service intelligence and outcome pricing — built once, monetized for decades. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in fleet connectivity/ota, service dispatch and parts, outcome/uptime contracts, with warranty analytics close behind. Volume grows on every path; the decision layer has not kept up. That gap is measurable, and it is the work.
For Industrial Equipment & Machinery, the queues and waits that come up first:

items: Machines in the field lack telemetry; service is reactive and parts planning blind.
Field service scheduling by phone and spreadsheet; first-time-fix suffers.
Cost per machine, contract profitability unknown; pricing tradition-based.
Connected machinery inherits product-security duties (EU CRA); firmware estates unmanaged.
Failure data accumulates without models; warranty and design loops closed by anecdote.
Dealer, parts and service systems disjoint; customer experience gaps.
